notes.meaning: God calls Ezekiel to speak as a prosecutor against Jerusalem, calling it the city of bloodshed. Repeating the question shows how urgent and serious the call to judge the city was. Ezekiel is told to lay out all of Jerusalem's terrible sins in the open, because the people had filled their streets with violence and murder.

The Lord warns that Jerusalem is bringing about her own ruin. By shedding innocent blood and worshiping idols, the city defiles itself and speeds up the day of its punishment. The very sins the leaders thought would help them actually ensure their downfall.

Jerusalem has made herself guilty of murder and filthy through idol worship, bringing her time of safety to an end. Because of this, God is making her an object of shame and mockery to nations both near and far. The surrounding countries laugh at her as a disorderly city that has lost all its honor.

The rulers and princes of Israel abused their power rather than protecting the people. Instead of upholding justice, each leader used his strength and authority to harm others and shed innocent blood.

The people in Jerusalem broke God's basic laws of love and family respect by treating their parents with contempt. They also took advantage of foreigners and cruelly cheated widows and orphans who had no one to defend them. God cares deeply about how we treat the vulnerable.
The city showed open contempt for everything God had set apart as sacred. The people neglected true worship and treated God's holy Sabbath rest days like ordinary working days.
Slanderers and gossips spread lies in order to get innocent people put to death. Others gathered at pagan mountain shrines to eat feasts honoring idols and commit shameful acts.

Ezekiel lists terrible sexual sins that broke the law of Moses and shattered family life. People ignored all moral boundaries through incest, adultery with their neighbors' wives, and violations of purity rules. These wicked deeds showed a society that had completely abandoned God's standards.

Judges and leaders accepted bribes to execute people, while lenders charged unfair interest and cheated their neighbors. At the root of all these crimes was one fatal failure: the people had completely forgotten the Lord. Forgetting God always opens the door to mistreating others.

God strikes His hands together as a sign of fierce anger against Jerusalem's dishonest money and bloodshed. He asks if their courage can hold up or if their hands will stay strong when He comes to deal with them. No human strength can stand against the Lord when He decides to act.

The Lord announces that He will scatter the people into exile among foreign nations to put an end to their uncleanness. By being scattered, Jerusalem will lose its special status as God's treasured possession and be shamed before the world. Through this painful discipline, the people will finally recognize that the Lord is God.

The word of the Lord compares the people of Israel to dross, which is the worthless scum left over when metal is refined. They used to be like precious silver, but now they are mixed and impure like scrap copper, tin, iron, and lead. In God's eyes, their moral decay made them useless.

Because the people have become like worthless dross, God gathers them into Jerusalem just like metal thrown into a furnace. As enemies surround the city, the heat of battle will be like a fierce bellows blowing on the fire. God's anger will melt their stubborn pride inside the besieged city.

God gathers the people together and blows on them with the fiery blast of His holy anger. Just as a silversmith melts metals in a hot furnace, the people will experience the intense heat of judgment in Jerusalem. Through this punishment, they will know without doubt that the Lord has poured out His wrath upon them.

God commands Ezekiel to describe the land of Israel as an unclean and neglected ground. In the day of God's anger, it is like a dry field that receives no rain to wash it clean or make it fruitful. The lack of rain was a visible sign that God had withdrawn His blessing because of their sins.

The corrupt leaders and false prophets banded together like roaring lions tearing their prey. They used their influence to swallow up people's property and rob them of their wealth. By urging the nation to resist Babylon instead of repenting, their lies led many men into battle and left behind countless widows.

The priests, who were called to guide the nation spiritually, broke God's law and treated His holy things as ordinary. They failed to teach the people the difference between what is sacred and common, clean and unclean. By ignoring the Sabbath, they caused God's name to be dishonored in the very place He was to be revered.
The rulers and nobles acted like ravenous wolves hunting for prey. Instead of protecting the weak, they destroyed lives and shed innocent blood just to grab dishonest wealth.

The false prophets covered up the rulers' crimes, like workers smearing cheap whitewash over a cracked wall. They told comforting lies and claimed, 'This is what the Lord says,' even though God had never spoken to them. Their deceit gave wicked leaders a false sense of peace.

Cruelty spread all the way down to the ordinary citizens, who robbed and cheated one another. They took advantage of the poor and mistreated foreign guests without any justice. When leadership fails, injustice quickly infects the whole community.

God looked for even one faithful person to rebuild the spiritual defenses and stand in the gap of the broken wall to pray for mercy. He wanted someone to intercede, like Moses once did, so the land would not be destroyed. Sadly, not a single leader or intercessor was found willing and able to turn back God's wrath.

Because there was no one to turn away His wrath, God poured out His indignation upon them like a consuming fire. He brought the consequences of their evil actions right down on their own heads. God's judgment was entirely just, giving the people exactly what their deeds deserved.
